relationship_to_restored_text: Interpretive contemplative layer aligned by verse. This does not replace the source-audited restored translation.

verses.mystical_translation: Benjamin's line begins again through Bela, Ashbel, and Aharah.
Nohah and Rapha complete the five sons in this version of memory.
Bela's household begins to unfold.
Three more sons continue the list.
Gera, Shephuphan, and Huram complete it.
Ehud's descendants are remembered through a relocation from Geba.
Gera moves households and fathers another branch, while the displaced people's experience remains untold.
Shaharaim begins a Moabite chapter after sending away two wives whose future is omitted.
Hodesh is named as wife and mother of a new household.
Her sons become heads of houses.
Hushim's sons remain in the genealogy despite her being sent away.
Elpaal's descendants build Ono and Lod, turning lineage into civic work.
Beriah and Shema lead Aijalon while Gath's residents are driven away.
Three names begin Beriah's longer household.
Three more continue it.
Michael, Ishpah, and Joha complete Beriah's sons.
Elpaal's descendants continue.
Three more sons are named.
Shimei's household begins with Jakim, Zichri, and Zabdi.
Elienai, Zillethai, and Eliel continue.
Adaiah, Beraiah, and Shimrath complete the branch.
Shashak's household begins.
Abdon, Zichri, and Hanan continue it.
Hananiah, Elam, and Anthothijah continue it.
Iphdeiah and Penuel complete Shashak's sons.
Jeroham's household begins with three names.
Jaareshiah, Elijah, and Zichri complete it.
The listed household heads live in Jerusalem.
Gibeon's household is remembered with Maacah named as wife.
Their sons begin with Abdon and include a son named Baal.
Gedor, Ahio, and Zechariah continue the household.
Mikloth's descendants settle among relatives in Jerusalem.
Saul's line is remembered through Jonathan, Malchi-shua, Abinadab, and Esh-baal.
Jonathan's line continues through Merib-baal and Micah, without shame attached to name or disability.
Micah's sons are remembered.
The genealogy continues through Ahaz, Jehoaddah, and Zimri.
Moza, Binea, Raphah, Eleasah, and Azel carry it onward.
Azel's six sons remain named.
Eshek's three sons form another branch.
Ulam's descendants close the chapter as archers and a large family, though neither war nor fertility defines their worth.

contemplative_note: Genealogy records who remained visible after relocation, divorce, exile, disability, and conflict. The contemplative reader listens especially for those whose futures are omitted: Hushim, Baara, people driven from Gath, and families moved by leaders. Memory becomes sacred when it refuses to confuse the survivor's silence with consent.
